name: discovery
description: Find out what a venue can do: adapters, operations and their schemas, published assets. Load on an unfamiliar venue or when no current tool fits.

content.inline:
## Discovery
What a venue offers, broad to narrow:
- read `{path: "v/info/adapters"}` — every adapter with its description and full operation paths (`v/info` also holds name, did, version, protocols).
- list `{path: "v/ops/<adapter>"}` browses one adapter's catalog; users publish their own ops under `o/`.
- asset-get `{id: "v/ops/..."}` returns an operation's full metadata — its `operation.input`/`output` JSON Schemas ARE the calling contract; read them before invoking an unfamiliar op.
- asset-list `{type?, offset?, limit?}` pages your own pinned assets.

Use what you find:
- Any discovered op is directly callable: give its full catalog path (or asset ref) as the tool name — dispatch resolves references, capability-gated as usual.
- On a REMOTE venue the same reads travel over grid: run `{operation: "v/ops/covia/read", input: {path: "v/info/adapters"}, venue: <did>}` (load the grid skill).
- Skills a venue offers: the skills op over its `v/skills` (see the skills skill).

Rules:
- `Capability denied` means permissions, not absence — an op can exist and be closed to you.
- Absence from a listing is not proof of absence either: explicit paths (e.g. `v/test/ops/...`) may still resolve.
